verdict.root_cause: The failing requests are intermittent ~15s stalls that terminate inside the frontend service: on the one error trace the span tree ends at a childless frontend/GET span whose entire ~15.0s is self-time, with no downstream ad, cart, product-catalog or DB span ever created [tr_a66c398ef4a0]. frontend-proxy merely propagates this (near-zero self-time) while its error ratio rises from an exactly-zero baseline to a bursty ~1.3% mean [tr_d02b69164bb6], and ad shows no error elevation of its own [tr_f7e513fb78fc] with only OTel exporter DNS failures in its logs [tr_2e10958165ec]. The ~15.000s round figure and the fact that a sibling frontend/GET branch in the same trace succeeded in ~2.6ms point to a subset of frontend request handlers hanging until a fixed client/proxy timeout, i.e. frontend is stalling on something it never emits a span for. No deploy or config change landed near onset for frontend or frontend-proxy [tr_f99438be7f9b], and flagd has no recorded changes and no logs [tr_deae37253e72, tr_b0da3459f23d], so the most likely mechanism is a flag-gated hang path in frontend rather than an artifact or config edit.
verdict.reasoning: Trace topology localizes the fault: the 15s is self-time in a leaf frontend/GET span with no children, which rules out every downstream service, DB and cache as the origin [tr_a66c398ef4a0]. frontend-proxy's own spans burn no time, so the proxy is a victim reporting the timeout, which also explains why it alerted first alongside load-generator. ad's alert is explained by it not being called on the failing paths (17 intervals with no recorded calls) rather than by ad erroring [tr_f7e513fb78fc], and its only log errors are telemetry-export DNS failures on the agent path, not request handling [tr_2e10958165ec]. The change log is empty in the 17 hours before onset for frontend and its one-hop neighbours [tr_f99438be7f9b] and empty entirely for flagd [tr_deae37253e72], which matches a runtime flag flip: no artifact and no config file changed. The intermittency (9 of 10 traces clean, a sibling branch succeeding in the same trace) fits a flag evaluated per-request far better than a bad artifact or a wrong config value, both of which would fail deterministically.
open_questions: No flagd metrics, traces or evaluation records were examined; the feature_flag attribution rests on absence of change records plus intermittency, not on a positive observation of a flipped flag.
frontend itself was never queried directly - no logs, metrics or change history for frontend's running state - so what the frontend/GET handler was blocked on during the 15s is unknown.
frontend-proxy emitted no logs at all for 32 minutes [tr_e20414659457]; whether that is a log-shipping gap or a sign the proxy itself is impaired is unresolved.
Only one error trace was sampled, so the 15s stall pattern may not be representative of all failing requests.

alternatives.root_cause: A frontend dependency (or an uninstrumented call such as a flag-store or cart lookup) became slow, and frontend hung waiting on it until the 15s timeout.
alternatives.why_not: No child span exists under the stalled frontend/GET at all [tr_a66c398ef4a0], so no instrumented downstream call was even attempted; attributing the wait to a dependency requires assuming an uninstrumented hop that no evidence names.

alternatives.root_cause: frontend exhausted a bounded resource (worker threads or connection pool slots), so a fraction of requests queued without ever starting downstream work and timed out at 15s.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and consistent with the childless stalled span, but no saturation, latency or resource metrics were collected for frontend, so nothing positively supports exhaustion over a flag-gated hang.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. The investigation should continue: the observable that would justify any action is a positive reading on frontend itself (frontend logs/metrics during a 15s stall, or flagd evaluation records showing a variant change at onset), none of which has been collected. Meanwhile the symptom to keep watching is frontend-proxy's error ratio, currently a bursty ~1.3% mean against an exactly-zero baseline [tr_d02b69164bb6], affecting roughly one request in a hundred.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is wrong if the stall is in fact a flag-gated code path that is cheaply revertible and is degrading real user traffic faster than the sampled 1.3% suggests. Two observations would falsify the abstention: (a) a flagd change record or evaluation log appearing for the incident window, which would satisfy revert_config's preconditions on flagd; or (b) frontend metrics showing the error ratio climbing monotonically rather than staying bursty, which would argue for acting on partial information. Note also that the effect of any fix here is only weakly observable - frontend-proxy emitted zero logs for 32 minutes [tr_e20414659457] and frontend was never queried at all, so confirmation would have to rest on span metrics and sampled traces alone.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued intermittent 15s stalls for a small fraction of user_get_ads requests. The risk of the alternative - proposing config_revert as the synthesizer named - is larger: revert_config requires both a prior configuration in change history and evidence of a config or flag change inside the window, and neither holds. flagd has no recorded changes whatsoever [tr_deae37253e72], and frontend's only recorded changes are four CART_ADDR edits that self-reverted 17.7 hours before onset [tr_f99438be7f9b]. Reverting frontend would therefore re-apply or disturb an already-settled CART_ADDR state, pointing frontend at a cart endpoint unrelated to the fault, and would recreate the container - converting a 1.3% intermittent failure into a brief total outage for a diagnosis that is explicitly low-confidence and rests on absence of evidence rather than a positive observation of a flipped flag. restart_service is equally unsupported: its precondition is evidence pointing at process state, and frontend's process state was never examined.
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal. For reference, had an action been taken on frontend, its callers in this incident are frontend-proxy and through it load-generator, with ad, cart and product-catalog seeing traffic stop and resume; an action on flagd would be seen by every service that evaluates flags against it, including ad.
proposal.notes: Abstaining because no permitted action's preconditions are met and the verdict's own confidence is low. The two open questions that would unblock a proposal are narrow and answerable: query frontend directly for logs, metrics and change history during the stall, and query flagd for evaluation records or metrics. Until one of those returns a positive observation, the feature_flag attribution rests only on intermittency plus the absence of change records - which is also consistent with a resource exhaustion, lock contention or connection-pool starvation inside frontend, none of which config_revert would touch.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service alerting spanning frontend-proxy, load-generator, and ad is not dismissible, and no open incident exists to fold it into. flagd as a one-hop candidate cause via ad weakly suggests a feature flag change, but evidence is absent.
